items.item_text: Background Check: Continued employment is contingent upon the completion of a satisfactory background investigation.
Live Scan Background Check: A Live Scan background check must be completed prior to the start of employment.
Bachelor's Degree from a four-year college or university or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience as a spokesperson for a high-profile institution in a large media market.
Experience managing crisis communications, including the development of emergency management and crisis communications plans.
10+ years full-time professional media experience, preferably in new media and/or television news.
Experience in writing op-ed and analysis pieces.

Leadership abilities that foster learning and excellence among team members. Supervisory skills to manage professional staff, including delegation and prioritization of work, training and evaluation. Experience planning and implementing employee professional development.

The Associate Director of Media Relations - Issues Management plays a critical role in UCLA's strategic communications efforts by supporting the management of sensitive, high-visibility issues and media inquiries. Working closely with campus leaders and key stakeholders, the position develops messaging, coordinates responses, monitors emerging issues, and helps execute communications strategies related to campus operations, public safety, student affairs, litigation, and other complex matters. This role combines media relations, issues management, crisis communications, and strategic advising to help ensure consistent, responsive, and effective communications that support UCLA's mission and reputation.
Demonstrated record of successful national, regional and local media relations planning, implementation and placement.
Solid professional judgment.
Excellent oral and written communications skills and ability to make professional presentations to executive-level participants in both group and one-on-one situations.
Working knowledge of the University, its organization and structure, and the roles and responsibilities of various academic and administrative units.
Demonstrated reporting and writing skills and ability to identify story placement opportunities and think strategically about communications, including social media applications.
Working knowledge of UC and UCLA policies, regulations, guidelines, and resources for programming.
Demonstrated ability to anticipate public events that can be used to advance institutional objectives.
Thorough knowledge and understanding of current events, issues and developments in the subject areas of institutional operations.
Knowledge of other issues facing public institutions of higher education.
Extensive media contacts at key ethnic, California and national media and ability to work with journalists at all skill levels, including student journalists.
Demonstrated knowledge of news media operations and protocols, especially the news gathering process.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with independent news media.
Superior strategic thinking, planning and program design and implementation skills.
Exceptional interpersonal skills to interact effectively with academic leaders, faculty, staff and external constituents.
Excellent organizational and project management skills and proficiency in prioritizing assignments to complete work in a timely manner and on deadline.
Demonstrated knowledge of software and multi-media applications, including systems that serve as tools for broadcasting news.
Ability to get to work reliably and on time and to be present in the workplace during normal working hours.
Ability to work evenings, weekends, and after hours as needed.
